description: Capabilities for the main window: the app's own native commands (timelog.rs) work without any entry here — Tauri v2 only gates plugin-provided commands — so this file exists specifically for the two plugins added for reliable file downloads (see src/lib/r2.js's downloadProtectedFile), plus two explicit window permissions for the exit-confirmation dialog (see main.js's wireCloseConfirmation) added 2026-09-21. core:default already includes core:window:default, which should cover close/destroy for the app's own main window on its own - these are listed explicitly anyway so the exit flow can never end up unable to actually close the window over an ACL gap that couldn't be fully verified against live Tauri v2 docs from this sandbox. dialog:allow-message was added 2026-09-22 so wireCloseConfirmation can use the dialog plugin's confirm() (a thin wrapper over the plugin's single 'message' command) instead of window.confirm(), which WebView2 silently fails to show when called from an async close-requested event instead of a direct click handler. core:window:allow-set-theme was added 2026-09-30 so the native Windows title bar can be switched to match the in-app light/dark toggle (see main.js's applyTheme) - without it the title bar stays light even when the rest of the app goes dark. The fs:allow-open/mkdir/exists/write + dialog:allow-open permissions were added 2026-09-30 for Meetings recording (src/lib/recorder.js) - streaming MediaRecorder chunks straight to a file on disk instead of holding a 3-hour recording in memory, plus letting the host pick any folder they want for it. Scoped to $VIDEO/** at first, then widened to "**" (any absolute path) 2026-09-24 after a real bug report: a folder picked on a different drive (G:\) failed with "forbidden path", because Tauri v2's fs scope is enforced per permission regardless of the bare unscoped permission also being listed, and $VIDEO/** never covered a drive/folder the host explicitly chose via the native folder picker. Widening only these four write-side fs commands (not the whole fs plugin) to "**" is an intentional tradeoff - the app already runs elevated (UAC) and the folder is always one the host picked themselves through an OS dialog, the same trust level as a Save-As dialog. Note: there is no fs:allow-close permission at all - a real GitHub Actions build (2026-09-24) errored with 'Permission fs:allow-close not found', confirming closing an already-open file handle isn't separately gated in Tauri v2's fs plugin (fs:allow-open covers the whole handle lifecycle) - don't re-add it. opener:allow-open-url was added 2026-09-24 for the 'Open in Google Calendar' button (main.js's downloadIcsForMeeting/openGoogleCalendarForMeeting) - opening an external https:// URL in the system's default browser is a SEPARATE command (plugin:opener|open_url) from opener:allow-open-path (which only opens local file/folder paths, e.g. Meetings recordings) - the two are not interchangeable. Also fixed a real bug the same round: the .ics download path was calling fs's writeTextFile, which has no matching permission granted here at all (only fs:allow-write-file, the binary variant r2.js's downloadProtectedFile already uses) - Tauri v2's per-command ACL silently rejected it, surfacing to the user as a bare 'something went wrong'. Switched to writeFile with a UTF-8-encoded Uint8Array, the same working pattern as r2.js, instead of adding yet another fs permission for a single one-off text write.
